originalText:
Max shipped almost 40 iOS apps that make a combined $36,000 a month. He built most of them after work, around a 9-to-5.

On camera he builds a new one, a stamp identifier, in under 20 minutes.

He starts in an ASO tool, not a code editor. His logic: 75% of App Store downloads start with a search, so the keyword is the problem people pay to solve. He types "stamp identifier", filters out crowded terms, checks the competitors, and finds only 4 apps ranked above 100, all released in 2025. Young niche, weak defenders. Keyword locked.

Then the part that took years to earn: his boilerplate. Onboarding, paywall, payments, settings, all prebuilt from 40 previous apps. On top of it he sends Claude Code a 2-sentence prompt: build the camera, gallery, identification, collection and history screens, make it compile. He waits. The app runs.

His money mechanics stay identical across the portfolio. Weekly subscription with a free trial plus a yearly, and a lifetime price for single-use apps. The review prompt fires at the aha moment, right after a successful scan, and never after a failed one.

Visuals take minutes: Gemini draws the icon, competitor screenshots feed the layout, the keyword goes into the title, subtitle and a stuffed 100-character list. Submit.

His advice cuts through the whole genre: thousands of AI apps flood the store every week, so make sure your AI slop beats theirs.

An app a week, after work. The keyword does the marketing.

Meta Quietly Launches AI Gaming App Pocket

https://t.co/EvWZdrzxIq
Meta has launched an experimental AI app called Pocket. The app lets users generate and share small interactive games using text prompts. 

These creations are called gizmos and can be browsed through a scrollable feed. Pocket stems from Meta's acquisition of the vibe-coded gaming platform Gizmo earlier this year. 

According to Appfigures data the app first appeared on the App Store and Google Play on June 29 2026. Reverse engineer Alessandro Paluzzi first spotted the launch on July 2 2026. 

The original Gizmo app remains listed and had generated 635000 lifetime installs across iOS and Google Play with 98% positive sentiment. 

Meta has not officially announced Pocket and has not responded to a request for comment.

originalText:
Google just shipped a dictation app that runs entirely on-device — no internet required, no audio leaves your phone.

Google AI Edge Eloquent is free on iOS and does something most transcription tools don't: it strips filler words ("um," "uh") in real time and smooths your phrasing before you see the text.

The offline mode runs on Google's Gemma architecture directly on your device. Connect your Gmail to import custom names and jargon. The Dictionaries tab lets you add niche terms manually.

Online features tap Gemini for deeper cleanup, summaries, and rewrite styles (formal, short, long). But the base experience works without any network.

Why this is interesting:
- Privacy-first: voice data never leaves the device
- Real-time filler word removal — not post-processing
- Speaking speed stats (WPM) + word count for communication improvement
- Free, with no subscription

The big question: will this come to Android? Right now it's iOS-only. If Google brings the same on-device Gemma stack to Android, this becomes a genuinely useful cross-platform tool.
